Rather than treating modern AI as a set of disconnected techniques, it frames intelligence as a coherent system of assumptions, objective functions, inductive biases, and evaluation logics that jointly determine what a model can learn, how it generalizes, and when its outputs can be trusted. Across five chapters, the book progresses from foundations and research design to explanatory statistical modeling and causal inference, then to predictive machine learning with explicit trustworthiness criteria, and finally to scalable data engineering lifecycles that make results reproducible in deployment.
